title: Largest open where h has P descends along the projection with section, for a groupoid whose source and target have R and a base change g having Q

statement_spans.label: author lemma environment with its own label lemma-local-source (no canonical tag in the snapshot tag list); statement at source lines 481-508

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: The first commutative diagram, whose squares are cartesian because the two maps t composed with pr_i from R times_U R to U are equal, is combined with the properties of diagram (equation-pull) to produce a second commutative diagram with cartesian squares relating pr_01 and pr_02 to c composed with (i, 1) and relating pr_1 and h to s. Assume s, t have R and g has Q. Then h has Q, being the composition of s, which has R hence Q, with a base change of g, which has Q; hence the largest open W(P, h) exists. By assumption (4) applied to the base change along the R-morphisms c composed with (i, 1) over s and t, the inverse images pr_01^{-1}(W(P, h)) and pr_02^{-1}(W(P, h)) agree, both being the largest open on which c composed with (i, 1) has P. The projection U' times_{g,U,t} R to U' has a section sigma sending u' to (u', e(g(u'))), and via the displayed identification of the fibre product over U' with U' times_{g,U,t} R times_{t,U,t} R the two projections agree with pr_01 and pr_02. The equality of the two inverse images therefore exhibits W(P, h) as the inverse image of a subset, necessarily the open W = sigma^{-1}(W(P, h)), which is the desired open subscheme of U'. (source lines 510-565)

standard_prerequisites.use: Its properties, combined with the first cartesian diagram of the proof, give the second commutative cartesian diagram identifying pr_01^{-1}(W(P, h)) and pr_02^{-1}(W(P, h)) as the largest open where c composed with (i, 1) has P.

core_obligations: Build the two cartesian diagrams: the first compares pr_01 and pr_02 over pr_1 for the triple fibre product, cartesian because the two maps t composed with pr_i agree; combining with diagram (equation-pull) yields a commutative diagram with pr_01, pr_02 mapping to h and c composed with (i, 1) to s, t, both squares cartesian (proof lines 511-538). Under the assumptions, h has Q as the composition of s, which has R and hence Q, with a base change of g, which has Q; hence W(P, h) exists (proof lines 541-545). Assumption (4) applied to the base changes along the cartesian diagram shows pr_01^{-1}(W(P, h)) = pr_02^{-1}(W(P, h)), both being the largest open on which c composed with (i, 1) has P (proof lines 545-548). The projection to U' has the section sigma : u' maps to (u', e(g(u'))), and under the displayed identification of the self fibre product over U' with the triple fibre product, its two projections agree with pr_01 and pr_02 (proof lines 549-559). The equality of inverse images then exhibits W(P, h) as the inverse image of a subset, necessarily the open set W = sigma^{-1}(W(P, h)), which satisfies W times_{g,U,t} R = W(P, h) (proof lines 560-564).
proof_roadmap: Assemble the two commutative cartesian diagrams from the groupoid axioms and diagram (equation-pull) (proof lines 511-538).
Show h has Q by composition and base change, so W(P, h) exists (proof lines 541-545).
Prove the invariance pr_01^{-1}(W(P, h)) = pr_02^{-1}(W(P, h)) via assumption (4) on the cartesian diagram (proof lines 545-548).
Descend along the section sigma and the identification of projections to obtain W with W times_{g,U,t} R = W(P, h) (proof lines 549-564).
